insights.ariaLabel: Information about the selected event type

facts.carrington: DONKI tracks Coronal Mass Ejections (CMEs) to help anticipate extreme scenarios. A solar storm similar to the 1859 Carrington Event could damage electrical grids and satellites today, so this data helps authorities protect critical systems.
facts.birthday: You can discover what the Sun was doing on the day you were born by selecting your birthday as the date range and exploring the solar events recorded on that day.
facts.mars: DONKI helps scientists study the effects of the solar wind on Mars. Because the planet does not have a strong global magnetic field like Earth, its atmosphere is more exposed to particles released by the Sun.
facts.astronauts: Space weather data helps protect astronauts by supporting radiation alerts for space missions and safety planning for future missions to the Moon.
facts.auroras: DONKI helps predict northern and southern auroras. Solar wind speed and geomagnetic activity can be used to estimate their likely intensity and location.

flr.whatIsHappening: The Sun releases enormous flashes of light and radiation. They travel at the speed of light and take only 8 minutes to reach Earth.
flr.howItAffectsYou: The radiation does not pass through the atmosphere, so we are safe, but it can disrupt radio signals used by aircraft and ships.

cme.whatIsHappening: A giant bubble containing billions of tonnes of magnetised gas is launched by the Sun into space.
cme.howItAffectsYou: When it travels towards Earth, it can push satellites out of their usual orbits and cause temporary disruptions to GPS signals on your phone.

gst.whatIsHappening: Energy from the Sun collides with and disturbs the invisible magnetic shield that protects planet Earth.
gst.howItAffectsYou: In extreme cases, it can overload electricity transformers and cause power outages. The positive side is that it can create spectacular auroras in the sky.

sep.whatIsHappening: A storm of extremely fast protons is released by the Sun, acting like a form of radioactive rain in deep space.
sep.howItAffectsYou: It is one of the greatest dangers for space travel. Astronauts on the Space Station or travelling to the Moon may need to take shelter in protected areas.

hss.whatIsHappening: The Sun has holes in its atmosphere through which a continuous stream of gases blows at millions of kilometres per hour.
hss.howItAffectsYou: It acts like the daily breeze of space. When this wind becomes stronger, it can trigger small auroras near Earth's poles.
